# Introducing Render Sandboxes: A computer for every agent

November 04, 2026

· Yaroslav Borets, Ammar Aijazi, and Azzam Aijazi

Today we’re launching Render Sandboxes in public beta. Render Sandboxes let you safely give your agents a computer to work with: a fully isolated Linux environment where they can install dependencies, edit files, and run code.

Each sandbox starts quickly, runs indefinitely, and automatically suspends when idle. You can reliably run thousands at once and lock down what each one can reach. You’re billed for CPU only when your agents are actually using it. [...] Render Sandboxes work with any agent harness and model. You can operate sandboxes through the TypeScript or Python SDK, or the Render CLI.

Check out our quickstart, or share this prompt with your coding agent:

## Agents need a computer of their own

Agents doing complex work need a separate machine for each task or user, isolated from your app and from each other. And since agent work comes in bursts, those machines need to start and stop with demand.

A web service isn’t built for this. Its instances stay up and serve all your users, and a new deploy can take minutes.

Render Sandboxes give each user or task its own machine the moment it’s needed. Each sandbox runs in its own Firecracker microVM.

“ [...] As agents become part of more products, giving each one a computer should be the easy part. We’re excited to see what this helps you build.

// The next day, restore it with memory and running processes intact.

snapshotId: checkpoint.id,

plan: checkpoint.plan,

render.com5 min read

Render has launched Render Sandboxes in public beta, providing isolated Linux environments powered by Firecracker microVMs for AI agents. The service enables agents to securely run code, install dependencies, and edit files while offering features such as filesystem and runtime snapshots, outbound network policies, and credential brokering. Billed based on actively used CPU, sandboxes are designed to scale from a single instance to thousands within a Render workspace.Open article →

Sandboxes are live on Render: a computer for every agent 🚀 I’m so stoked to share what we’ve been building. If you’re building with agents, you know they need their own space to do real work, isolated from your app and from each other. That’s exactly what Sandboxes gives them, and they’re fast and cheap to run. Here’s what I love about it from a Design point of view: Sandboxes has two users. There’s the developer setting it up, and the agent working inside it. That changes what “interface” even means. The SDK, the CLI, the docs, a prompt you paste straight into your coding agent... nobody’s clicking through most of these, and they still deserve craft. We brought that same thinking to the landing page. Instead of telling you what a sandbox does, it shows you one spinning up, running a [...] a sandbox does, it shows you one spinning up, running a task, taking a snapshot, and shutting down. (Watching infrastructure work is weirdly satisfying, I promise.) So proud of the whole team for shipping this. It’s in beta, which means your feedback actually shapes what comes next.
